assumptions: The endpoint is mounted at the application root as `/ping`, not behind any existing API version prefix (e.g. `/api/v1`), because it is meant to be a trivially reachable liveness probe.
`/ping` is public: it must be excluded from any global authentication/authorization dependency, API-key check, or rate-limiting middleware the app applies to other routes.
It is a pure liveness check with no dependency probing — it does not touch the database, cache, or any downstream service, and always returns 200 with a static body.

The route belongs in the existing health/system router if one exists; if the codebase has no such router, a new `health` router module is created and included in the app rather than defining the route inline in the app entrypoint.

tasks.description: Locate the FastAPI application entrypoint (e.g. `main.py` / `app/main.py`) and the existing router layout. Add a `GET /ping` route to the existing health/system router; if no such router exists, create one (e.g. `app/routers/health.py` following the project's existing router conventions) and include it on the app with no prefix so the final path is exactly `/ping`. The handler takes no parameters and returns the literal JSON body `{"pong": true}` with HTTP 200.

Ensure `/ping` is reachable without credentials: if the app applies a global auth dependency (`FastAPI(dependencies=[...])`, an auth middleware, or a router-level dependency), add `/ping` to its exempt/whitelist path list alongside any existing exempted paths such as `/health`, `/docs`, or `/openapi.json`. Do the same for any global rate-limiting middleware. If no global auth or rate limiting exists, make no changes and note that in the PR description.

Add a test in the project's existing test suite (using `TestClient`/`httpx.AsyncClient` consistent with current tests) that calls `GET /ping` and asserts status code 200, `response.json() == {"pong": True}`, and that the request succeeds with no auth headers supplied.

Polish the OpenAPI surface and docs: give the route an explicit `response_model` (or `responses` schema) and a `summary`/`tags` value matching the conventions used by neighbouring routes so it renders sensibly in `/docs`, and add a one-line entry for `GET /ping` to the API endpoint list in the README or existing API documentation.
